questions.question: What practical limits did a tribune's power to intervene have?
options: It applied only to patrician citizens
It worked only during wartime
It expired after thirty days in office
It required the Senate's approval each time
He had to be present and it reached only about a mile beyond the city
questions.explanation: Because the tribune's power rested on putting his sacrosanct body in the way, he had to be physically present. His authority reached only about a mile beyond Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: That brought limits: he had to be physically present to intervene, and his authority reached only about a mile beyond the city.

questions.question: How many commissioners did Gaius Terentilius Arsa propose to define and restrict the consuls' powers?
options: Five
Ten
Three
Two
Twelve
questions.explanation: Terentilius proposed five commissioners in 462 BC. The patricians stalled for years, citing war and plague.
questions.sourceQuote: He proposed appointing five commissioners to define and restrict their powers.

questions.question: What detail in official lists of consuls casts doubt on the traditional story of the conflict?
options: They show no consuls at all before 449 BC
They include men with plebeian family names in the 5th century BC
They include Greek names from Athens
They record consuls elected by the Plebeian Council
They list only one consul per year
questions.explanation: Men with plebeian family names appear as consuls when the office was supposedly closed to plebeians. Another oddity is how little bloodshed such bitter grievances produced.
questions.sourceQuote: Official lists of consuls include men with plebeian family names in the 5th century BC, when the office was supposedly closed to plebeians.

questions.question: Who killed Verginia to save her from Appius Claudius Crassus?
options: Verginia herself
Her betrothed, a tribune
Her brother
A crowd in the Forum
Her father, Lucius Verginius
questions.explanation: Her father, the respected centurion Lucius Verginius, killed her to prevent her rape. Riots then spread from the city to the army camped outside.
questions.sourceQuote: To save her from that fate, her father killed her himself.

questions.question: Who were the first tribunes of the plebs, for 493 BC?
options: Lucius Albinius Paterculus and Gaius Licinius
Appius Claudius Crassus and Lucius Verginius
Lucius Valerius Potitus and Marcus Horatius Barbatus
Agrippa Menenius Lanatus and Tarquinius Superbus
Gaius Terentilius Arsa and Volero Publilius
questions.explanation: Lucius Albinius Paterculus and Gaius Licinius were the first tribunes. They soon chose Sicinius and two others as colleagues.
questions.sourceQuote: The first tribunes, for 493 BC, were Lucius Albinius Paterculus and Gaius Licinius, who soon chose Sicinius and two others as colleagues.

questions.question: By 457 BC, who assisted the ten tribunes of the plebs?
options: The college of pontifices
Two plebeian aediles
Two patrician quaestors
Four Senate envoys
The two consuls
questions.explanation: The ten tribunes were helped by two plebeian aediles, assistants who also had to be plebeians. Ancient writers disagree on whether there were originally two or five tribunes.
questions.sourceQuote: By 457 BC there were ten, helped by two plebeian aediles, assistants who also had to be plebeians.

questions.question: Under Table IV of the Twelve Tables, what happened to a son sold three times by his father?
options: He went free
He was adopted by the buyer
He was sent to the army
He lost his citizenship
He became a slave for life
questions.explanation: Table IV gave fathers vast power over their families, but a son sold three times went free. The laws as a whole were practical and often harsh.
questions.sourceQuote: Table IV gave fathers vast power over their families, though a son sold three times by his father went free.

questions.question: Under the Lex Publilia of 471 BC, how would plebeians now meet and vote?
options: By centuries of the army
By curiae
By wealth classes
By tribe, the districts in which citizens were registered
By family clans
questions.explanation: The reform had plebeians meet and vote by tribe, and tribunes were elected the same way. This broke patrician influence and made the plebs politically independent.
questions.sourceQuote: Plebeians would now meet and vote by tribe, the districts in which citizens were registered, and tribunes would be elected the same way.

questions.question: Which two senators restored the tribunes and the right of appeal after the decemvirs fell?
options: Lucius Valerius Potitus and Marcus Horatius Barbatus
Lucius Sicinius Vellutus and Lucius Verginius
Gaius Terentilius Arsa and Volero Publilius
Lucius Albinius Paterculus and Gaius Licinius
Agrippa Menenius Lanatus and Appius Claudius
questions.explanation: Valerius and Horatius restored the tribunes and the right of appeal in 449 BC. As consuls, they went on to pass further laws on plebiscites.
questions.sourceQuote: Two senators, Lucius Valerius Potitus and Marcus Horatius Barbatus, restored the tribunes and the right of appeal.

questions.question: What condition did the Senate attach to its offer in 457 BC to increase the number of tribunes?
options: That the Plebeian Council be dissolved
That none of the old tribunes stand again
That patricians could also become tribunes
That the tribunes serve without pay
That the veto be abolished
questions.explanation: The Senate offered to raise the tribunes to ten provided none of the old ones stood again. The plebs had been re-electing the same tribunes for five years to keep up pressure.
questions.sourceQuote: In 457 BC the Senate offered a trade: the number of tribunes would rise to ten, provided none of the old ones stood again.
